$comment: Registry for the model benchmark workflow (.github/workflows/eval-benchmark.yml), separate from e2e/matrix.json so adding a benchmark model never adds a CI check. `models` are slots: a stable `name` (`<lab>-high`, `-mid`, and `-low` tiers per major lab where the lab offers a current model for the tier, plus each open-weight family's main model; `openai-low` is eve's default model) and the gateway `id` that currently fills it. Bump a slot's `id` when its lab ships a successor; records keep both, and the pinned release marks the change. Leave out service-tier variants (`-fast`) unless they are eve's default. Each slot runs every listed fixture `attempts` times against the local world; each id must exist in the AI Gateway catalog, which pins its release. `mockWorlds` run each `mockFixtures` entry (default: every fixture; it may also name fixtures scripted for the mock model that no live leg runs) `mockAttempts` times with mock models: `local`, a world with a package in e2e/matrix.json (a local production server), or a matrix world with no package (`vercel`: a preview deployment per leg, run one at a time). An entry `{ name, fixtures }` limits a world to some mock fixtures; keep hosted lists short, since each leg deploys. Mock legs cost only runner time, and their timings are the primary framework-overhead signal; the `vercel` legs are the only ones that see hosted Workflow round trips. Leave out of `mockFixtures` any fixture whose evals are all tagged `real-model`, since its mock legs would run nothing. `devStartup` runs `eve dev` (to ready and a first turn), `eve build`, and `eve start` `runs` times for each named agent in `subjects` that packages/eve/scripts/benchmark-startup.mjs generates (`minimal`): run 1 starts from an empty project (cold), later runs reuse its caches (warm). `concurrency.legs` caps live legs running at once (gateway load); `concurrency.evalsPerLeg` is passed to `eve eval --max-concurrency` on every leg, overriding a fixture's own maxConcurrency, so evals do not share a runner. Both change measured latency, and each run's manifest records them.
